step1_analysis.description: A double-balanced Gilbert cell mixer used in a transmitter front-end to up-convert an intermediate frequency (IF) or baseband signal to a radio frequency (RF) using a local oscillator (LO). It features inductive degeneration for linearity and an LC tank load tuned to the RF frequency.

paper_reference.title: A Silicon Bipolar Transmitter Front-End for 802.11a and HIPERLAN2 Wireless LANs

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the mixer circuit.

sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports 2W for the entire multi-stage transmitter power amplifier. A single mixer stage in SKY130 typically consumes 5-15 mW depending on the tail current.

conversion_gain.description: Ratio of the RF output voltage amplitude to the IF input voltage amplitude.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain ≈ (2/pi) * gm * R_load. With gm ≈ 20mS and R_load ≈ 500 ohms (LC tank at resonance), Gain ≈ 6.3 V/V = 16 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Mixer conversion gain is typically lower than the full TX chain gain. 10-20 dB is standard for an active Gilbert cell with a tuned load.

operating_frequency.description: The target RF output frequency of the up-converter.

sky130_expected.calculation: f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L_total * C_total)). With L=4nH and C=230fF, f ≈ 5.2 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The LC tank (L3, L6, C1) must be tuned to the 802.11a standard frequency of 5.2 GHz.

supply_voltage.description: DC supply voltage required for operation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Standard nominal VDD for SKY130 1.8V devices.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adapted from the paper's 3V bipolar process to the 1.8V SKY130 CMOS process.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power consumption and transient conversion gain of the Gilbert cell up-converter. The NPN transistors are mapped to SKY130 NMOS devices, and the output center tap is connected to VDD.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Gilbert Cell Up-Converter Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* DUT (NPNs replaced with SKY130 NMOS for CMOS adaptation)
I1 n3 GND 5m
L1 n3 n9 1n
L2 n3 n8 1n
L3 n6 n7 2n
C1 n6 n10 230f
* L4 n7 GND (Original netlist shorted center tap to GND. Changed to VDD RF choke)
L4 n7 VDD 10u
L5 label_net_0 GND 1n
X1 n10 n2 n1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=10u l=0.15u
L6 n7 n10 2n
X2 n6 n2 n5 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=10u l=0.15u
X3 n10 n0 n5 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=10u l=0.15u
X4 n1 label_net_1 n8 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=20u l=0.15u
R1 n2 n4 1k
R2 n0 n4 1k
L7 n0 n2 5n
X5 n5 label_net_2 n9 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=20u l=0.15u
X6 n6 n0 n1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=10u l=0.15u

* Power Supply
V1 VDD GND 1.8

* Biasing
Vbias_LO n4 GND 1.2

* Existing Testbench DC Sources (with series resistors to prevent inductor shorts)
VLABEL_NET_0 label_net_0_src GND 0.9
R_src0 label_net_0_src label_net_0 50
VLABEL_NET_1 label_net_1 IF_ac_p 0.9
VLABEL_NET_2 label_net_2 IF_ac_n 0.9

* IF Signal (200 MHz Baseband/IF)
VIF_p IF_ac_p GND dc 0 sin(0 0.01 200Meg)
VIF_n IF_ac_n GND dc 0 sin(0 0.01 200Meg 0 0 180)

* LO Signal (5 GHz Local Oscillator, AC Coupled)
VLO_p n2_ac GND dc 0 sin(0 0.3 5G)
VLO_n n0_ac GND dc 0 sin(0 0.3 5G 0 0 180)
C_LO_p n2_ac n2 1p
C_LO_n n0_ac n0 1p

.control
  * DC Operating Point for Power
  op
  let power = -i(V1) * 1.8
  print power

  * Transient Analysis for Conversion Gain
  tran 10p 20n
  
  * Measure IF input peak-to-peak amplitude
  meas tran if_max max v(label_net_1, label_net_2) from=10n to=20n
  meas tran if_min min v(label_net_1, label_net_2) from=10n to=20n
  let if_pp = if_max - if_min

  * Measure RF output peak-to-peak amplitude (at 5.2 GHz)
  meas tran rf_max max v(n10, n6) from=10n to=20n
  meas tran rf_min min v(n10, n6) from=10n to=20n
  let rf_pp = rf_max - rf_min

  * Calculate Conversion Gain in dB
  let conv_gain = rf_pp / if_pp
  let conv_gain_db = 20 * log10(conv_gain)
  print conv_gain_db
  
  quit
.endc
.end
